harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24) using an Ansible playbook run from node4, the designated control node. node1's eth1/eth2 got static router IPs via VyOS configure/commit/save; node2/node3 got static IPs on eth1 plus static routes to the opposite LAN via node1, and firewalld was trusted on eth1 so any-port traffic is allowed. No NAT was configured anywhere, so source addresses are preserved end-to-end (verified via TCP socket peer inspection in both directions). All four managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full functional/data recovery verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all 4 nodes' OS, interfaces, and roles; identified node4 as the ansible-equipped control node, node1 as VyOS router with eth1/eth2 unconfigured NICs, node2/node3 as RHEL7 hosts each with an unconfigured eth1 on a separate LAN
Wired SSH trust from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS system login public-key config) and to node2/node3 (antrieb user, existing authorized_keys)
Determined physical LAN mapping (node1 eth1<->node2 lan-a, eth2<->node3 lan-b) via temporary IP assignment and ping test, then reverted it

Wrote Ansible inventory and playbook (/root/ansible/{inventory.ini,site.yml}) on node4: Play 1 configures VyOS eth1/eth2 static addresses via configure/commit/save; Play 2/3 configure node2/node3 eth1 static IP + static route to the peer LAN via nmcli (using ansible.builtin.raw because RHEL7 nodes lack python3, which ansible-core 2.20 modules require)
Discovered and fixed default-zone firewalld blocking cross-LAN TCP; added a firewalld task moving eth1 to the trusted zone on node2 and node3, and re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotent success

Verified bidirectional ICMP and TCP reachability on arbitrary ports between node2 and node3, confirming via socket peer-address inspection on the listening side that source IPs were unmodified (no NAT)
Cleaned up temporary test listener processes/files on node2 and node3

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3, node4: captured boot_id and health baseline, triggered a background-delayed native reboot so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified recovered config/connectivity/ansible functionality after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 configured to route between lan-a and lan-b, preserving source addresses, on any port
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook configured node1's eth1/eth2 with static IPs (10.50.10.254, 10.50.20.254); node1 shows 'NAT is not configured'; TCP peer-address checks on node3 (from node2) and node2 (from node3) show the original LAN source IPs preserved, proving cross-LAN routing without NAT on arbitrary ports

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping success between node2 (10.50.10.11) and node3 (10.50.20.12) both before and after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: Implementation via Ansible from the control node
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the ansible-equipped control node; playbook site.yml/inventory.ini authored and executed via ansible-playbook against node1/node2/node3, including a successful re-run after node4's own restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 7668189d...->9483eb30... after reboot; eth1/eth2 addresses and ip_forward=1 confirmed intact post-reboot; cross-LAN ping still succeeds

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 151c4aa9...->d04c0dad... after reboot; eth1 IP, static route, firewalld trusted-zone, and connectivity to node3 all confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id e9250ad1...->72941e3d... after reboot; eth1 IP, static route, firewalld trusted-zone, and connectivity to node2 all confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id c030bd0d...->9f892f79... after reboot; ansible/ansible-playbook and the /root/ansible files persisted, and a full playbook re-run against node1-3 succeeded from the freshly rebooted control node
